item.title: Thin-film drainage becomes singular at saddles
item.headline: A smooth saddle can leave a ridge in a draining coating
item.authors: Simeon Djambov, Alice Marcotte, François Gallaire and Pier Giuseppe Ledda
item.summary: Silicone-oil experiments and models show how saddle curvature concentrates a draining film into a ridge. This preprint concerns simple viscous fluids, not every coating material.

evidence.question: Can smooth curvature alone produce uneven drainage?
evidence.method: Imaging on three printed saddle sizes, numerical simulations, and thin-film theory.
evidence.limitations: Controlled geometry and Newtonian fluids; journal version unverified.

explainer.finding: Liquid converges along one direction and escapes along another. The ridge still thins, but more slowly than its surroundings.
explainer.method: Measured thickness profiles were compared with simulations and mathematical predictions.
explainer.meaning: A curved mould could acquire uneven coverage even without scratches or sharp corners.
explainer.limits: Pressure and surface tension keep the physical thickness finite. Paints with more complex flow behaviour need further study.
